South Carolina Gamecocks.oc: Kendal Briles, hired after Mike Shula was dismissed nine games into 2025.
South Carolina Gamecocks.oc_status: New — the guide records the in-season change from Shula to Briles, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
South Carolina Gamecocks.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator. The guide does not name the incoming coordinator and says only that the defense needs some rebuilding but has been consistent under Beamer.
South Carolina Gamecocks.play_caller: New. The guide states Beamer has nine offensive starters back and a new play-caller, and identifies Briles as the man taking over.
South Carolina Gamecocks.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide describes Briles as having a long record of good offenses and of maximizing quarterbacks, and says he must fix the passing game and use LaNorris Sellers' skill set better.
South Carolina Gamecocks.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy, but the guide documents a usage shift it wants reversed: Sellers had 49 designed carries in 2025 against 79 in 2024, even though the underlying quality held at 4.64 yards after contact, 25 runs of 10-plus yards and 5.3 yards per attempt.
South Carolina Gamecocks.qb_development: Attributed to the incoming coordinator rather than the head coach. The guide credits Briles with a long record of maximizing quarterbacks and says it is genuinely curious how he uses Sellers.
South Carolina Gamecocks.continuity: Head coach and quarterback return; both coordinator positions change. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 4 for the quarterback, totalling 11.
South Carolina Gamecocks.staff_turnover: Substantial and partly mid-season. Shula was dismissed nine games in, Briles was hired, and the Stability Score table also records a defensive coordinator change.
South Carolina Gamecocks.portal_recruiting: Not addressed in guide as a staff-driven effect.
South Carolina Gamecocks.vsin_assessment: Credit for the coach, doubt about the trajectory. The guide calls Beamer a coach who has shown he can get the most from a roster and summarises the programme as intriguing, then asks how sturdy the ground beneath him is: he signed an extension in January 2025 after a nine-win season, went 4-8, has a second losing season in three years, has not won a bowl since his first season, and has watched a very talented quarterback appear to regress under him. It acknowledges that raising the alarm on a coach locked in through 2030 may seem premature, then asks whether another poor season heats his seat enough to leave South Carolina rudderless by year's end.
South Carolina Gamecocks.strengths: A head coach the guide credits with maximizing rosters and with defensive consistency, nine returning offensive starters, and a coordinator hire with a record of good offenses and of getting the most from quarterbacks.
South Carolina Gamecocks.concerns: Two coordinator changes at once, a 4-8 season immediately after an extension, no bowl win since 2021, a quarterback whose decline the guide calls stark, and a slate of defenses ranking among the nation's best.
South Carolina Gamecocks.betting: The guide ties its outlook to the coaching change without turning it into a stated market edge: it stacks its doubts as questions about whether Sellers' regression is real, whether Briles can restore his 2024 form, and how the offense measures against the schedule, then closes by noting even six wins would be an improvement.

Tennessee Volunteers.dc: Jim Knowles, hired to run the defense.
Tennessee Volunteers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Tennessee Volunteers.dc_status: New — the guide records Knowles being hired to run the unit, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Tennessee Volunteers.play_caller: Josh Heupel on offense, whom the guide rates an elite play-caller. It applies the same description to Knowles on defense.
Tennessee Volunteers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide's repeated characterisation is that the system is user-friendly and has a high floor, which is why annual quarterback churn has not disrupted it.
Tennessee Volunteers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Tennessee Volunteers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated tendency.
Tennessee Volunteers.qb_development: Addressed as a pattern rather than a claim about individual development: Heupel has started a different quarterback in Week 1 of every season at Knoxville, and Tennessee has averaged at least 31.8 points per game every season under him regardless. The guide expects freshman growing pains from Faizon Brandon and frames the move as being about the programme's future.
Tennessee Volunteers.continuity: Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinator and quarterback both change. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 0 respectively, totalling 10.
Tennessee Volunteers.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive side, where Knowles was brought in. The guide separately records heavy player losses on defense: all four defensive line starters plus three rotation players, and two secondary starters, one of them an NFL draft pick.
Tennessee Volunteers.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the coaching staff. On the roster the guide records linebacker Amare Campbell arriving as Penn State's leading tackler in 2025.
Tennessee Volunteers.portal_recruiting: Not addressed in guide as a staff-driven effect. Recruiting is addressed at quarterback: Faizon Brandon is a five-star and the third-ranked member of the 2026 class.
Tennessee Volunteers.vsin_assessment: Steadiness rather than peaks. The guide notes the 2024 playoff exit to Ohio State as a high point, says the Heupel era has had no true lows, and shapes 2026 as another perfectly adequate season. It is deliberately measured on upside — an SEC title-game push is called unlikely — while allowing that if the true freshman quarterback hits, Tennessee is a sneaky team with more upside than most expect.
Tennessee Volunteers.strengths: An elite offensive play-caller with a scoring floor of 31.8 points per game across his tenure, a system the guide calls user-friendly, offensive-coordinator continuity, an offensive line that lost one starter and is a Joe Moore Award contender, and an elite defensive play-caller now running the other side.
Tennessee Volunteers.concerns: A true freshman quarterback, and a defense that must rebuild its entire line and part of its secondary under a coordinator in his first season with the programme.
Tennessee Volunteers.betting: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, and the guide rests it on the head coach: Heupel's consistency — at least eight wins in four straight years, and 7-5 in the regular season in the one year he missed that mark — plus immense offensive talent giving a firm floor despite the quarterback question.

Texas A&M Aggies.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide credits Mike Elko with a strong record at both Duke and Texas A&M.
Texas A&M Aggies.oc: Not addressed in guide by title. The guide names Holmon Wiggins as the new offensive play-caller.
Texas A&M Aggies.dc: Not addressed in guide. Elko is described as a defensive mastermind.
Texas A&M Aggies.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator. See the conflicts field: the team page describes a new offensive play-caller.
Texas A&M Aggies.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Texas A&M Aggies.play_caller: New on offense. The guide lists a new offensive play-caller among the obstacles and names Holmon Wiggins, leaving open whether the change aids Marcel Reed's development.
Texas A&M Aggies.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide characterises Elko's units as consistently well above average and records 21.0 points per game, 4.2 yards per carry and 5.1 yards per play allowed, all top-25 marks.
Texas A&M Aggies.qb_development: Left open rather than asserted. The guide sets out Marcel Reed's passing limitations in detail and says a new play-caller arrives, then explicitly declines to say whether that aids his development.
Texas A&M Aggies.continuity: Strong but not complete. Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback all return per the Stability Score table (p. 44), which prints 4, 3, 0 and 4 with 4 points for 18 returning starters, totalling 15 — the defensive coordinator is the change.
Texas A&M Aggies.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide beyond the new offensive play-caller and the coordinator points printed in the Stability Score table.
Texas A&M Aggies.prior_school: Duke, where the guide credits Elko with a strong record before Texas A&M. On the roster it records First Team All-AAC linebacker Ray Coney being added.
Texas A&M Aggies.portal_recruiting: Not addressed in guide as a staff-driven effect. The guide records the roster as the 13th-most experienced in the country.
Texas A&M Aggies.vsin_assessment: Respectful and unconvinced about the ceiling. The guide credits Elko with improving the Aggies' record every year and calls him a defensive mastermind who always maximizes talent, then sets the size of the task against it: a very difficult schedule, a new offensive play-caller, and the goal of a first SEC championship and possibly a first modern national title. Its conclusion is pointed — Elko will have to do more than maximize talent to reach championship level.
Texas A&M Aggies.strengths: A head coach with year-on-year improvement at two programmes, defensive units the guide calls consistently well above average, eight returning defensive starters and the 13th-most experienced roster in the country.
Texas A&M Aggies.concerns: A new offensive play-caller inheriting a quarterback with pronounced passing limitations, a new defensive coordinator per the Stability Score table, the loss of three defensive linemen to the NFL — which the guide calls a massive blow — and a very difficult schedule.
Texas A&M Aggies.betting: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins, argued as potential versus reality: Reed has not shown real progress in his weak areas, and the defense is good but not among the SEC's elite. The guide separately notes Texas A&M is tied with Alabama at DraftKings to win the SEC at +850 and 20-1 for the national championship, and poses the upside case that the market may be underrating what Elko could build in a season loaded with parity.
Texas A&M Aggies.conflicts: The guide states the offensive coaching situation two ways. The team pages (pp. 312–313) list a new offensive play-caller among the obstacles and name Holmon Wiggins as the man arriving, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator. Both are reproduced as printed and neither is corrected.

Texas Longhorns.dc: Will Muschamp, hired to run the defense.
Texas Longhorns.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Texas Longhorns.dc_status: Returning per the Stability Score table (p. 44), which awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator. See the conflicts field: the team page records Muschamp being hired to run the defense.
Texas Longhorns.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name for 2026. The guide credits Steve Sarkisian with taking Quinn Ewers to the playoff two seasons ago and winning two games there.
Texas Longhorns.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide records Texas ranking 66th in defensive success rate against the pass and 33rd in opponent EPA per play through the air, and expects overall improvement under Muschamp.
Texas Longhorns.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy. The guide records the 2025 run game as limited at 4.2 yards per carry and 138 yards per game and expects more push behind a rebuilt line.
Texas Longhorns.qb_development: Addressed only through precedent and expectation: the guide cites Sarkisian taking Quinn Ewers to the playoff, and its case for Arch Manning rests on his own late-season form — 14 touchdowns over the final six games with a 1.2% turnover-worthy play rate and 7.8 yards per attempt — rather than on a stated development record.
Texas Longhorns.continuity: Complete as printed. The Stability Score table (p. 44) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 3 for 16 returning starters — totalling 17, among the highest in the guide.
Texas Longhorns.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide beyond the hiring of Muschamp to run the defense.
Texas Longhorns.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Wake Forest right tackle Melvin Siani arriving as the standout portal addition.
Texas Longhorns.portal_recruiting: Sarkisian added offensive line bodies through the portal, with Siani the standout, and the guide records five-star cornerback John Meredith III — ESPN's top-ranked 2027 corner — reclassifying into the 2026 cycle to enroll in the fall.
Texas Longhorns.vsin_assessment: Confident in the coach. The guide notes sixteen returning starters, among the most experienced rosters in the country, says the biggest weakness — the offensive line — has been addressed, cites Sarkisian taking Ewers to the playoff two seasons ago and winning two games there, and states it would be shocking if he cannot get this roster to the field.
Texas Longhorns.strengths: The highest tier of continuity the guide's own table records, a head coach with a playoff run to his name, a rebuilt offensive line, and a defensive hire the guide expects to bring overall improvement.
Texas Longhorns.concerns: A quarterback who barely completed 60% across the full season and ranked eighth among conference passers by PFF grade, and a secondary that lost three starters after middling pass-defense rankings.
Texas Longhorns.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. The guide's coaching-linked claim is confidence in the roster and staff rather than a stated price edge.
Texas Longhorns.conflicts: The guide states the defensive coaching situation two ways. The team pages (pp. 310–311) record that Will Muschamp was hired to run the defense, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator. Both are reproduced as printed and neither is corrected.

Vanderbilt Commodores.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records that Clark Lea returned to his alma mater.
Vanderbilt Commodores.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Vanderbilt Commodores.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Vanderbilt Commodores.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Vanderbilt Commodores.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide calls the 2025 defense underrated at 3.7 yards per carry and 22.8 points allowed, 23rd in opponent EPA per rush and 49th in success rate on the ground, with the secondary the weakness at 129th in EPA per dropback and 111th in success rate.
Vanderbilt Commodores.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy. The guide records a productive 2025 ground game — 176 yards per game at 5.6 per carry — and expects a stark drop-off once Diego Pavia's 862 rushing yards and a rebuilt line are accounted for.
Vanderbilt Commodores.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide notes Lea says there will be a competition and that five-star freshman Jared Curtis appears the likely starter, and cautions that equally talented quarterbacks have struggled in less demanding circumstances than the SEC.
Vanderbilt Commodores.continuity: Strong on the staff, broken at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4 for the head coach, 3 for the offensive coordinator, 3 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 3 for 13 returning starters, totalling 13.
Vanderbilt Commodores.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Vanderbilt Commodores.prior_school: Vanderbilt itself — the guide notes Lea returned to his alma mater. On the roster it records former four-star Ricardo Jones arriving from Clemson.
Vanderbilt Commodores.portal_recruiting: Lea added portal bodies in the secondary including Jones, but the guide says he expects considerable internal promotion. It records only one FBS transfer added to an offensive line that lost four starters.
Vanderbilt Commodores.vsin_assessment: Credit for what has been built, and a stated expectation of decline. The guide says Lea achieved what he returned to his alma mater to do — 17 wins in two seasons and a first bowl win since 2013 — then frames the test as doing it without a superstar quarterback, with a true freshman starting, an offensive line to rebuild, and a schedule offering both opportunity and misfortune. It states plainly that decline, even for one season, is on the horizon.
Vanderbilt Commodores.strengths: Full coordinator continuity, a head coach the guide credits with a genuine programme turnaround, an underrated run defense and seven returning defensive starters, mostly in the front seven.
Vanderbilt Commodores.concerns: A true freshman quarterback behind a wholly rebuilt offensive line, and a secondary the guide says could again be among the country's worst. It puts the doubt as a question — beyond the front seven, which Vanderbilt unit can be trusted?
Vanderbilt Commodores.betting: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. The guide explicitly acknowledges this may be an overly pessimistic reading, then lists why it holds: a freshman quarterback behind a wholly rebuilt line, and a secondary that could again be among the country's worst. The coaching link is the staff continuity being asked to absorb both losses at once.
